Applies to all blank pages. Pages with a photo keep their own layout (change it on the page itself).
Double-sided print alignment  ▸

Crop marks are on by default. Each sheet gets trim guides that run to the paper edge (line the guillotine up to a guide, at any scale) and a dashed center line (the fold/spine).

When printing, set Scale to 100% (not "Fit to page"). There's a 9 mm safe margin so the crop marks stay clear of your printer's unprintable edge and always appear.

Two things to line up:

  • Crop marks = the fixed frame. Same spot on every sheet, never move when you nudge.
  • Grid lines = the panel boundaries (the dashed lines between page-boxes). These are what must match front-to-back.

Align front vs. back:

  1. Print a two-sheet test, hold both up to a light.
  2. Slide them so the crop marks stack (corners on corners, fold on fold).
  3. Now check the grid lines. If sheet 1's don't sit on sheet 2's, note the gap: too far left → nudge right; too high → nudge down.
  4. Nudge (0.5 mm/click). The grid moves, the crop marks stay put. Reprint and re-check.
  5. If the back is tilted or stretched (not just shifted), use Rotate / Scale.

Done when: crop marks stacked → grid lines overlap. Then cut to the corner marks, fold on the dashed line, stack, staple.

If the front is rotated or stretched vs the back (not just shifted), use Rotate (0.1° steps) and Scale (0.1% steps). Reset returns everything to zero.

Define your own fold template  ▸

Each grid is one physical printed sheet; each cell is one panel. Pick your book size (8 or 16 pages), then assign a page to every panel and tick upside-down where the fold needs it. For a 16-page single-sheet zine, use 4 columns × 4 rows on one sheet — the I-cut fold (works on any paper; A3 gives the largest pages, A4/Letter make a smaller book); for a saddle-stitch booklet use two sheets. The built-in “16-page zine (I-cut)” in the Format menu is a ready-made starting point.

Save & export
How it works ▸

Tap a slot to upload a photo, or drag & drop onto it. Once placed, drag to pan and scroll to zoom.

Reorder: in the top strip, long-press a page tab then drag it to a new spot (or use the ← → buttons on the page). A quick swipe still scrolls the strip. Undo/redo with the arrows or ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z.

Use the toggle on interior pages for one portrait or two stacked horizontals. On any photo (interior or cover), the ▣ / ⤢ button switches between Fill (crop to fill, pan to reposition) and Fit (show the whole photo with margins).

On the covers, tap the blank area to add a photo. Click a text box, the QR code, or a photo to select it — the panel at the bottom sets its font, colour, size, QR link, and photo (including Replace / Remove photo). Drag the box itself to move it, or use the ✥ handle — a single tap still lets you edit the text.

Open the menu (top-left) for format, paper, templates, alignment, and export.
